name: Kirron Kher
role: Indian actress and BJP member of the Lok Sabha for Chandigarh (2014–2024)
summary: Kher combines support for business-led development and social insurance with explicit advocacy for LGBT protections and equal marital authority. Her parliamentary record favors severe penalties for rape, preservation of traditional crafts and uniform divorce law; she also welcomed revocation of Kashmir’s special status.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Calls for universal cashless health insurance covering outpatient as well as inpatient treatment.

cut-welfare.rationale: Insists that social spending and subsidies remain necessary while expanding employment.

state-harmful.rationale: Assigns government an essential role in development and social protection.

empower-police-military.rationale: She welcomes the larger home-affairs budget, asks the government to approve the police-modernisation scheme to 2020 and demands restored benefits for soldiers' children; she asks for funding, not new powers.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defends handloom protections as necessary to preserve Indian cultural inheritance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Supports an industrial policy steering development toward green IT and other non-polluting businesses.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Opposes replacing protected handloom production with mass mechanization despite cheaper output.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Rejects assigning women domestic work and men earning roles.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Explicitly describes Indian society as patriarchal and discusses women’s systematic disadvantage.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Supports government social security, health insurance, education and poverty programs.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Affirms equal rights regardless of caste, religion, gender or sexual preference.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Explicitly calls for uniform divorce law instead of unequal religious personal-law protections.

population-transfer.rationale: Condemns the forced departure of northeastern students and displacement of Kashmiri Pandits.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Condemns Emergency-era imprisonment of opponents and suppression of the press as intolerance.

party-controls-media.rationale: Criticizes the muzzling of the press during the Emergency.

death-penalty.rationale: Explicitly defends capital punishment for repeat rapists.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Rejects religious justification for withholding married women’s civil protections.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Proposes extending employment, housing and service protections to the wider LGBT community.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Defends enforceable marriage obligations and legal protection against unilateral abandonment.

religious-nation.rationale: Rejects dividing Indians by religion and affirms that all born in India belong.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Champions plural voices in 2015, but later backs preventing allegedly divisive campus agitation; the boundary is unclear.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Explicitly champions self-perceived identity and legal protections for transgender people.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combines support for business expansion with public insurance and anti-poverty spending.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Defines marriage as equal power and mutual respect, rejecting patriarchal male control.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Rejects recognition of religious rules that subject women to injustice.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Rejects lesser punishment for repeat rapists; her stated rationale favors mandatory severity in that context.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Identifies religious divorce practices as a source of women’s subordination, while defending religion’s compassionate ideals.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Welcomes revocation of Jammu and Kashmir’s special autonomous status.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Wants artisans equipped with modern marketing technology while preserving traditional craftsmanship.

notes:
No views are attributed from her party, husband, film roles or questions merely requesting ministerial information. Her CAA support does not establish a desired numerical immigration reduction. LGBT advocacy does not establish a position on same-sex marriage. Solar expansion and non-polluting industry priorities do not by themselves establish support for drastic climate measures. Criticism of a rape survivor’s transport choices does not establish a legal dress restriction. Remaining null statements reviewed across all ten themes; no corresponding nuclear, AI, monetary-system or international-governance position was found. Later available material did not establish reversals of the quoted policy positions. Her opposition to gender stereotypes does not by itself establish that gender is primarily constructed. Private religious practice does not establish a policy on religion’s overall public role.
